_comment: What counts as the same word in this pack, and what does not.
The fold decides whether a written answer is marked right, so it needs
fixtures on both sides: pairs that MUST compare equal, and pairs that MUST
NOT. An over-eager fold marks wrong answers right forever, and nothing else
in the test suite would notice.
Greek folds every diacritic away — accents, breathings and the iota
subscript alike — because a student typing on a plain keyboard gets those
wrong long before they get the word wrong. Final sigma folds with them, so
a word compares equal to itself wherever it sat in the sentence.
The price is real and is written down here rather than discovered later:
ἀγορά/ἁγορά and εἰμί/εἶμι are distinct words in print and this pack cannot
tell them apart. A tutor that accepts a missing breathing is the trade; a
pack that wanted them kept would set stripMarks to the accents alone.
